parsed.why: Equality law covers gender identity and borders are ordinary, but a 150-person mob attack on trans people, discontinued police-mistreatment complaints, male-default custody with transfer route, and reserved social climate keep it out of low risk.

Constitutional protection and self-ID coexist with systemic birth-sex prison placement reaching a foreign national, documented custody violence and deaths, and murder responses judged inadequate — tier-1/tier-2 exposures offsetting strong formal law.

Sodomy law sporadically enforced, documented police as a main source of violence against trans people, victims framed as perpetrators, widespread stigma and near-zero accountability; only third-gender traditions and a sanctuary village mitigate.

Total-control regime leaving no space for LGBT life, undefined morality provisions at official discretion, documented executions, forced concealment, no recognition, no recourse. Thin data here reflects suppression, not safety; structural facts imply catastrophic exposure.

Visitors report little direct hostility and courts blocked bathroom exclusion and surgery mandates, but no anti-discrimination statute, family-register custody with documented mistreatment of a detained trans person, and bathhouse/ward-document friction hold it below top tier.
